implementation_notes: Java has no named or default parameters, so the local idiom is lambda configuration: pass `Consumer<Builder>` / `UnaryOperator<Config>` (or `Function<Config, Config>`) values that each change one setting, and let the factory apply them over a defaults instance - the shape used by RecordBuilder's `with(b -> b.age(200).name("whatever"))` and Immutables' lambda initializers. Records with wither methods (Java 16) give the immutable form: `ServerConfig.DEFAULT.withPort(9000)`. The classic Go structure (an option function type plus With* constructors) can be hand-written, but the pervasive alternative remains the GoF Builder, and records cannot express omitted components, so defaults live in static factories or withers.
pitfalls: A configuration lambda mutates a mutable builder, so partially configured state is visible during construction and an exception leaves a half-built instance; validate in build() and never share the builder between threads.

Wither chains allocate one throwaway object per step and lean on the garbage collector; Sonar's builders/withers/records guidance recommends a single builder pass when many fields change in a hot path.

Records do not express optionality: the canonical constructor requires every component, so `new ServerConfig(null, 8080, null)` is a legal invalid instance - defaults belong in static factories, withers or a builder.
A lambda's target type must be a functional interface; overloads taking `Consumer<T>` and `UnaryOperator<T>` for the same method cause ambiguous lambda errors at the call site.

variants.name: Record with wither methods (Java 16)
variants.implementation_notes: A `record` is the shallowly immutable carrier for a configuration, and wither methods (`withPort(int)`) are small copy-constructors that return a modified instance; a static DEFAULT constant carries the library defaults. Records give value equality, a stable toString for logging and a canonical constructor that can validate and defensively copy. Withers keep the option vocabulary named at the call site without a builder class, and are what RecordBuilder/Immutables generate when a record grows past a few components.
pitfalls: A wither per component is O(n) code; beyond a few components the class of withers becomes boilerplate and an annotation processor (RecordBuilder) or a builder becomes the better trade.
The canonical constructor must be re-entered on every wither, so validation runs per step and deep option chains cost O(n) allocations.
Compact canonical constructors can validate but cannot supply defaults; if defaults are needed the record needs a static factory or a builder, which reintroduces the pattern it replaced.
